2026-11-12.title: Second Thursday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-12.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: He who has the bride is the bridegroom
2026-11-12.verse: He must increase, but I must decrease.
theo: Paul feels “a divine jealousy” for the Corinthians: “I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” The apostle is like the friend who brings the bride to the bridegroom; he fears that she will be led astray to “another Jesus”.

John the Baptist says the same about himself: “He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom… rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice.” Every true minister in the Church points away from himself to Christ. Holiness is this: he must increase, I must decrease.
outline: Ask: do people meet Christ through me, or only me?
The Church is a bride kept faithful to one Lord.
Point 2 · The friend of the bridegroom
Ministers bring the bride to Christ, not to themselves.
Joy in letting Christ be first.
live: Let someone else take the credit today.
Avoid one source of teaching that leads you from the faith.
2026-11-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, keep us faithful to you alone. Let me rejoice to hear your voice; you must increase and I must decrease. Amen.

quick: The Church is betrothed to Christ alone.
True ministers point to Christ, not themselves.
2026-11-12.action: Let someone else take the credit today.
2026-11-12.question: Where do I need to decrease so Christ can increase?

homily: Dear friends, Paul says he feels a divine jealousy for the Corinthians: I promised you in marriage to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ (2 Corinthians 11:2). The apostle is like the friend who brings the bride to the bridegroom.

John the Baptist describes himself in the same way: he who has the bride is the bridegroom; the friend of the bridegroom rejoices greatly at his voice. He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:29–30).

This is the motto of every Christian and every minister: he must increase, I must decrease. In the parish and in the family, let attention turn not to me but to Jesus. Today do one good deed that no one knows about, and give the glory to Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: Jesus must become greater, I must become less. Today do one good thing that nobody sees, just for Jesus!

intro: Paul and John the Baptist both bring the bride to Christ and step aside with joy.

sub: God remembers Israel's first love in the desert.
The Church is called to that faithful love.
q: I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice.
points.apply: Renew your first love for Christ in prayer.

sub: God takes his people as bride in faithfulness.
Paul guards the Church from “another Jesus”.
q: I will take you for my wife in faithfulness; and you shall know the LORD.
For this reason my joy has been fulfilled.
points.apply: Hold fast to the faith of the Church.

q: Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Let someone else have the credit today.

concl: The Church belongs to Christ alone.
Let us rejoice to hear the Bridegroom's voice.
2026-11-12.resolve: Pray each morning this week: “Lord, you must increase.”
